check_service_status.description: Check whether the Studio Ghibli API is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being asked to slow down is reported separately from being down. No API key required.
check_service_status.display_str_template: Check the Studio Ghibli API status.

mock_response.message: The Studio Ghibli API is up and lists 7 species.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

online.description: Whether the service answered with a usable species list.

rate_limited.description: Whether it asked this workspace to slow down.

reachable.description: Whether it answered at all. A service that is reachable but not online is refusing or misreporting rather than down.

response_time_ms.description: How long the answer took, in milliseconds.

species_count.description: How many species it listed, or empty when it did not answer with any.

status_code.description: The HTTP status it answered with, or empty when it could not be reached.

get_film.description: Get one Studio Ghibli film by its title, its Japanese or romanised title, its id or its URL: the plot, director, producer, release year, running time, Rotten Tomatoes score and poster, plus every character, species, place and vehicle the catalogue links to it, each with its name and id. No API key required.

description: Browse the worlds of Studio Ghibli through the free, keyless Studio Ghibli API: every film from Nausicaä to The Boy and the Heron with its plot, director, release year, running time, Rotten Tomatoes score and poster, and the characters, species, places and vehicles of each one. Look a record up by name or id, list a film's cast, find every cat in the catalogue, or pick a film of the day that stays the same all day. Numbers come back as numbers and every link carries the record's name and id, so a workflow reads the answer rather than decoding it. No account and no API key: connecting takes one click.
